title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): a 'magasin' (store of multistructures) is a set M with three relations. X <= Y is read as 'X is a face of Y'. X << Y is read as 'X is contained, as a closed cell, in Y'. X |o| Y is read as 'X and Y have disjoint open parts'. The axioms are: Mag 1, both <= and << are orders and <= implies <<. Mag 2, if X << Y there is a smallest face of Y containing X (the carrier); X o<< Y means this carrier is Y itself, i.e. X meets the interior of Y. Mag 3, |o| is symmetric and irreflexive and stable under passing to X' o<< X. Mag 4, distinct faces of one cell have disjoint interiors. On the previous page X ≭ Y ('X and Y meet properly') is defined: every face of X that is not a common face is |o|-disjoint from every face of Y that is not a common face.

This page defines the (irreducible) figures of M:

F_M = { L ⊂ M : L is downward closed for <= and X ≭ Y for all X, Y in L }.

Combinatorially, a figure is a cell complex assembled from cells of the store: closed under taking faces, with any two cells meeting properly along common faces.

Two optional restrictions are announced:
(1) finiteness or local finiteness;
(2) a 'polyhedral' condition: if X, Y are in L and X~ ∩ Y~ is non-empty, then this intersection is a single principal ideal Z~, i.e. Inf(X, Y) exists. This is the intersection axiom of polytopal / regular cell complexes.

M embeds in F_M by X ↦ X~ = M_{<=X}, the 'elementary figures'. This map is injective and order-preserving. That X~ is a figure uses Prop 1 of the next page: ≭ is reflexive and stable under passing to faces.

The relations are extended to figures, writing F~ for the set of X with X~ ⊂ F, i.e. X ∈ F:
- F <= G iff F ⊂ G. Inf is intersection; Sup is union when it exists.
- F << G iff every X in F lies << some Y in G. On elementary figures this restricts exactly to the old <<: if X << Y' <= Y then X << Y.
- F ≭ G iff X ≭ Y for all X in F and Y in G. This is equivalent to {F, G} being bounded above in F_M, to Sup(F, G) existing, and to F ∪ G being a figure.

Purpose: build, from the purely combinatorial 'store' of cells, the poset of all polyhedral-type figures (the 'canonical ...' associated with M). This is a step in the 1986 combinatorial-axiomatic rewriting of tame topology / Analysis Situs (GF VIII).
errors: No genuine error. The statement that elementary figures X~ belong to F_M is used here, but its justification (reflexivity of ≭ and stability under faces) is only proved on the next page as Prop 1. The sentence 'Sup ... est ∪' should be read as 'when it exists'; this is consistent with the later equivalences. The chain of equivalences F≭G ⇔ bounded above ⇔ Sup exists ⇔ F∪G ∈ F_M is correct, because any downward-closed subset of a figure is a figure.

ideas.what: Figures as downward-closed, pairwise 'properly meeting' subsets of an abstract store of cells
ideas.modern_name: abstract (polyhedral/regular CW) cell complex as an order ideal of a face poset; subcomplex of a cell poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; abstract cell complexes (Tucker, Steinitz), face posets (Björner); polytopal complexes (Ziegler)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic 'géométrie modérée' / Analysis Situs ideas in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Polyhedral condition: the intersection of two cells is a single common face (Inf exists)
ideas.modern_name: intersection property of polytopal / polyhedral complexes; meet-semilattice condition on face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology (e.g. Rourke–Sanderson, Ziegler)

ideas.what: The poset of figures F_M: intersections always exist; sups exist exactly for pairwise compatible families; compatibility is binary
ideas.modern_name: consistently (coherently) complete poset / cliques of a coherence-type relation; ideal-completion-like embedding X ↦ principal ideal
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott domains (Scott 1970s), coherence spaces (Girard 1987), Plotkin's coherent domains

ideas.what: Extension of the containment relation << from cells to figures, compatible with the embedding

missed.claim: F_M has the structure of the down-closed cliques of a binary compatibility relation. It is closed under intersections, and under unions of pairwise compatible families, with 'bounded ⇔ pairwise compatible ⇔ union is a figure'. This is the coherent-domain / coherence-space pattern that Girard made central in linear logic one year later (1987), here arising from cell-complex geometry. It is a mild structural parallel and not a deep result.
missed.quote: F ≭ G ⇔ ∀X∈F̃, Y∈G̃, on a X≭Y ⇔ {F,G} majoré dans F ⇔ Sup(F,G) existe dans F ⇔ F∪G ∈ F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could help frame Grothendieck's 'magasins' (an unpublished axiomatics of tame/polyhedral structures) in domain-theoretic terms. It is of mostly historical interest.

missed.claim: The 'magasin' axiomatics of tame topology (cells with face, containment and interior-disjointness relations, and figures built from them) is an unpublished attempt at a purely combinatorial foundation for Analysis Situs. It is close in spirit to later o-minimal cell decompositions and abstract stratified/cell posets, but its specific form was never developed in the literature.
missed.quote: On sera amené, à l'occasion, de faire sur les figures envisagées deux types possibles de restriction 1°) ... 'finitude' ... 2°) ... 'polyédrale'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical documentation of how Grothendieck intended to realise the 'géométrie modérée' programme of the Esquisse. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary definitions, all correct, inside an unpublished axiomatic framework ('magasins'). The framework is of historical interest, but this page contains no non-trivial result, and the domain-theoretic parallel is mild.
transcription_corrections: 'On étend : f les relations d'ordre ≤ et ≪' should read 'On étend à F les relations d'ordre ≤ et ≪ de M (en plongeant M dans F via les "figures élémentaires" X̃, X ∈ M)'.
Bottom-left margin: the definition is most likely F̃ = {X ∈ M | X̃ ⊂ F} (i.e. X ∈ F), identifying elements of M with elementary figures.

Left-margin note: 'Notation canonique' is doubtful. The word before 'canonique' is a noun naming F_M (possibly 'Nébuleuse' or similar), so the note reads 'F_M sera appelé [?] canonique associé(e) au magasin M'.
'(irréductibles)' at the top is an insertion qualifying 'figure' in the first line: 'On appelle figure (irréductible)...'.

In the paragraph on the embedding, the struck-out/garbled part reads roughly: '...injective et préserve le ≤-ordre, ce qui identifie M à une partie de F_M (... les figures élémentaires, X ∈ M : la figure élémentaire associée ...)'.
